thread:
zoe: dropped a new prototype for playground structured-output/tool-card density. two axes: verbosity (full args vs badge-summary) and action layout (single primary + inline secondary vs compact overflow). feedback plz. https://figma.com/file/mock

matt: initial read: compact overflow looks cleaner in dense lists (run history) but might hide important arg defaults.

ria: agree with matt. one idea: show a tiny summary line with arg types + default indicator, e.g., "title (string), timeout=30s". keeps card short but gives context.

aria: accessibility: any collapsed area must expose a visible keyboard affordance. aria-expanded on chevrons and announce when defaults exist: "3 args, 1 default". Also color contrast for badges needs check.

zoe: copy question: primary CTA label — we use "Invoke" across the console. Should the tool-card CTA be "Invoke" or context-aware like "Invoke with defaults"?

matt: prefer consistent single word: "Invoke". show secondary helper text under the card when defaults differ.

ria: microcopy test idea: run a small 2x2 test across density x CTA variant: Invoke vs Invoke with args. measure click-through and error rate when args missing.

ux-bot: quick poll started  vote for CTA: Invoke, Invoke with args, Run, Start. react to vote.

matt: :thumbsup: Invoke

aria: :white_check_mark: Invoke with args

ria: :point_up: Invoke (consistency win)

zoe: also prototyping keyboard helpers: show hint in the shortcut overlay and add a 1s focus ring delay to avoid jitter when many cards mount. snippet proposed:
```
K -> jump to next card primary action
Enter -> invoke focused action
Shift+K -> previous card
```

aria: test that with NVDA/VoiceOver. make sure focus management doesn't trap in dense lists.

zoe: next steps: I'll iterate on badge-summary variant (show arg count + short type list) and a hybrid action layout (primary + 3-dot overflow). I'll attach updated mocks and a small moderated session plan. thanks for quick takes!
